mcq.QUESTION_DESC: Why do pipelined architectures favor simple addressing modes?
How does fixed-length instruction encoding help pipelining?
For a 5-stage pipeline, which instruction set feature reduces structural hazards?

sq.ANSWER: RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computer) instruction sets are better suited for pipelining because they have simple, fixed-length instructions that complete in a uniform number of cycles. This consistency allows the pipeline to progress smoothly without stalls caused by instruction complexity. In contrast, CISC (Complex Instruction Set Computer) instructions are often variable-length and may take multiple cycles, making pipeline design more complicated and prone to hazards and delays.
sq.QUESTION_DESC: Why are RISC instruction sets better suited for pipelining compared to CISC?

sq.ANSWER: Instruction dependencies in instruction sets cause data hazards in pipelining because later instructions may need results from earlier ones that have not yet completed. If the instruction set contains many instructions with frequent dependencies or complex addressing modes, it can increase pipeline stalls. Therefore, instruction sets influence pipeline performance based on how often dependencies occur and how easily they can be detected or avoided through instruction scheduling.
sq.QUESTION_DESC: How do instruction dependencies in instruction sets affect pipelining?

lq.ANSWER:
Instruction sets vary from Complex Instruction Set Computers (CISC) with many complex instructions to Reduced Instruction Set Computers (RISC) with a smaller, simpler instruction set.

Effect on Architecture:

  • CISC:

    • Complex instructions perform multiple low-level operations in a single instruction.

    • Often microprogrammed control to handle complexity.

    • Benefits: Compact code, easier assembly programming.

    • Drawbacks: Longer execution cycles, complex decoding, and harder pipelining.

  • RISC:

    • Simple, uniform instructions usually executed in a single cycle.

    • Hardwired control for speed.

    • Benefits: Simplified pipeline design, easier hazard handling, higher clock rates.

    • Drawbacks: More instructions per program, potentially larger code size.

Influence on Processor Design:

  • RISC favors pipelining and parallelism.

  • CISC may require complex control and microprogramming.

Summary:
Instruction set complexity directly guides architecture choice, affecting performance, hardware complexity, and code density.
